questions.q: Describe the seasons of India's monsoon climate.
answer: India has a tropical monsoon climate, marked by the seasonal reversal of winds, and the year has broadly four seasons.

answer.text: Cold and mostly dry, with the northern plains coldest; the north-west gets some rain from western disturbances and the south-east from the retreating monsoon.
Hot, with dry scorching winds called the loo in the north, and low pressure building over the land.
The main rainy season, when moisture-laden winds from the Arabian Sea and Bay of Bengal bring most of India's rainfall.
The monsoon withdraws, giving humid weather and rain to the south-east coast.

questions.q: Explain the main factors that affect the climate of India.
answer: Several factors together shape India's climate and cause it to vary from place to place.

answer.text: The Tropic of Cancer passes through the middle of the country, so the south is generally hotter and more tropical than the north.
Higher areas are cooler, and the Himalayas shield the plains by blocking cold winds from Central Asia.
Coastal areas have a moderate, maritime climate, while the interior has a more extreme, continental climate.
Mountains such as the Western Ghats force moist winds to rise, bringing heavy rain on the windward side and leaving a dry rain shadow on the leeward side.
